How to practise at home

  1. Pick five or six words, not the whole list. A few words done well beat a long list done once.
  2. Say a word, let your child look at it, then cover it and ask them to write it from memory.
  3. Check letter by letter. Ask which part was tricky, and circle that part.
  4. Come back to the tricky ones the next day, then a few days later. Short and often works best.
  5. Let your child read the word back to you. If it sounds odd to say, that is usually the tricky part.

Questions

Is this list statutory?
Yes. The Years 5 and 6 word list is statutory: it is set out in English Appendix 1 of the national curriculum for England. Pupils are expected to be taught these words across the two years, alongside others the teacher chooses.
Where does the list come from?
From "The national curriculum in England - English Appendix 1: Spelling" (Department for Education, 2013-09), published on GOV.UK. We copied the words as printed and checked them against two other copies; GOV.UK wins if they differ.
Is it free?
Yes. There is nothing to buy or sign up for to read, print or use this page.
Are there ads or tracking?
No. This page has no ads, no analytics, no cookies and makes no requests to other websites.
Why does a word have two spellings, like busy/business?
The curriculum prints some entries together because they are related (for example eight/eighth). Each form is shown so your child can practise both.
